subject: Scoping of reactive dependencies, reactive rain checks

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: Scoping of reactive dependencies, reactive rain checks
parts:
Hi

  I'm daresay that reactive depdendency tracking is done using dynamic scoping - that is to say if a reactive value (input) is consumed then the nearest reactive on the (parent frame) stack is assumed to have caused it.

  In R, I can evaluate functions in the scope of the caller.  For instance, to allow me to specify which specific columns in xtable are 'sanitized', I create a magic function which can see the internals of xtable:

noSanitize<-function(exclude)function(col){
 xtableLogic <- substitute(
  {if (names(x)[i] %in% exclude) col else sanitize(col)},
  list(exclude=exclude,col=col))
 eval(envir=parent.frame(),xtableLogic)
}

  I'm considering building an R asynchronous GET to streamline parallel fetches from shiny server to restful apis (and other ajax).

  For this I may require telling the caller of the asynchronous get that it should be re-evaluated, using the invalidatelater reactive.

  This is probably the wrong way to do it, but I want the user interface to be pretty (if not clean :) and want to explore some ideas.

 output$foo <- reactivePlot({ plot(parallelGet(input$url)) })

  How does the shiny reactive dependency tracker understand this?

  Would exceptions be a better way?

  stop(setClass(list(state="not ready",delay=ms(1)),"reactiveRainCheck"))

  (having shiny core understand this message to mean it should try the reactive again soon)
 
  Perhaps monads and infinite lists are a better idea, but I don't know where those are up to (if anywhere)

-Alex

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Scoping of reactive dependencies, reactive rain checks
parts:
I talked to Alex in person about this, but for anyone who is curious, something like option 2 makes a lot more sense to me given the reactive primitives we have today:

values <- reactiveValues()
parallelGet(input$url, function(result) {
  values$data <- result
})

output$foo <- renderPlot({ plot(values$data) })
